title: Worked open-access cancer reference review (validation + teaching artefact + pivot fallback)
context: The project's pivot/fallback deliverable (if no pilot review team is secured by ~2027-03-31) is a complete, openly-licensed, worked systematic review on open-access cancer literature produced with the tool. This reference review serves three purposes: (1) validation — it proves the tool works on a real review and demonstrates recall, extraction accuracy, and PRISMA conformance; (2) a teaching artefact — it shows methodologists and potential partners how to use the tool correctly; (3) pivot deliverable — if no pilot team is secured, releasing this review as a methods artefact constitutes a real output to the cancer research community. The review must be methodologist- and oncology-reviewed, with all licence/provenance controls applied. Depends on 014 (RoB assist) and 015 (PRISMA reporting). Cancer guardrails apply fully: open-access/aggregate/de-identified data only.
objective: Conduct and document a complete, openly-licensed systematic review on a cancer topic (e.g. a rare cancer such as Ewing's sarcoma or a paediatric oncology topic) using the tool: define a registered protocol (PICO + PROSPERO registration or equivalent), import and screen open-access records via the tool's ingest and screening workflows, extract data using the extraction assist, assess risk of bias using the RoB assist, generate PRISMA artefacts, and produce a report that is methodologist- and oncology-reviewed and released under CC-BY-4.0.
acceptanceCriteria: A registered protocol (PICO question, inclusion/exclusion criteria, outcome definitions, PROSPERO id or equivalent) is defined and committed to the repository before screening begins

Records are sourced from open-access databases (PubMed/MEDLINE metadata, PMC Open Access full text, or equivalent); all sources are verified via the rights gate (task 005) with licences recorded before ingest

The full screening workflow (title/abstract + full-text) is conducted using the tool; the AI screening assist proposes but humans confirm all dispositions; the audit log records every disposition with the human actor; recall on the review's included set is reported

Data extraction is conducted using the extraction assist with all values in proposed-unverified state until human-committed; the gold-standard extraction sheet (task 009 fixture) is updated or a new one created from this review
Risk-of-bias assessment is conducted using the RoB assist; humans assign all ratings; the RoB evidence and ratings are recorded in the provenance store
PRISMA 2020 artefacts are generated (flow diagram with reconciled counts, report scaffold, screening log export, extraction dataset export with licence/attribution manifest, reproducibility manifest)
The completed review document is reviewed and signed off by a methodologist (systematic-review methodologist) and an oncology-evidence reviewer before publication
The review document and dataset are released under CC-BY-4.0 with full attribution to sources and reviewers
output: A complete, openly-licensed worked systematic review on an open-access cancer topic produced using the tool: registered protocol, screening log, extraction dataset with provenance, risk-of-bias assessment, PRISMA 2020 artefacts, reproducibility manifest, and the final review document — all methodologist- and oncology-reviewed and released under CC-BY-4.0.
